name: recurring_charge_currency_price_digit
doc:
The charge-currency `price_dig` for one instrument family.

Replaces the last use of `OKTBiz.createChargeConvertorWithInstFamily:` in the Recurring
buy-price sheet, which read `.quotePrecision` off the returned convertor to cap the text
field's decimals.

The equivalence is exact for spot, checked in the source rather than assumed:
`OKTSpotCommon.createChargeConvertorWithInstFamily:` (`OKTBiz.m:1575-1580`) builds
`OKTSimpleChargeConvertor` with `precision: cc.priceDig.integerValue`, where `cc` is
`getChargeCurrencyForInstFamily:` — the same charge currency and the same `price_dig`
that [`resolve_price_digit`] reads. So `quotePrecision == price_dig` on this path, and
the two price funnels above already round at that digit.

`0` for an unresolved family, which is native's own number there rather than a chosen
default. `createChargeConvertorWithInstFamily:` never returns nil — it allocs
unconditionally, so a missing charge currency reaches `cc.priceDig.integerValue`
through ObjC nil-messaging and yields `precision: 0`.

Do NOT continue that sentence into "so the Swift `?? 2` beside the read only ever
covered a missing spot-biz OBJECT, a branch with no analogue once `OKTrade` is gone".
That inference is what dropped the cushion and shipped the P0: it compares the two
VALUES and ignores the two STORES. Native's biz is warmed before the running-bots list
renders (`OKTStrategyLiveOrdersDataSource.m:541` calls `loadBiz:` per order inst type),
so its `0` was near-unreachable. core-trading's spot biz is warmed on the Rust detail
screen (`info_stream_use_case.rs` awaits the preload) but by nothing on the
running-bots-list route, which is where `0` became the usual answer.

Value parity is not behaviour parity when the two sources are warmed differently.

`0` also keeps the absence semantics of the two funnels above, so those two cannot
disagree with each other. That is NOT a whole-screen invariant: a caller that takes the
input-cap variant below deliberately breaks it — iOS's buy-price sheet caps at 2 while
its market-price label still renders at 0.

## Do not use this one to cap a text field

The `0` is a display convention, and applying it to an input cap is what
produced a P0: the buy-price sheet locked its fields to zero decimals AND
prefilled the saved bounds rounded to integers, so a stored 0.42-0.87 range
opened as 0-1 and Confirm submitted that (iOS `9e78f4423`, reachable from the
running-bots list, which primes nothing). `0` is also a legitimate digit for
an integer-priced instrument, so the caller cannot tell the two apart here.
Use [`recurring_charge_currency_price_digit_warmed`], which waits for the
store and answers `None` when the family genuinely did not resolve.

name: RecurringCoinRatio
doc:
One coin in the plan being edited.

# Why the ratio is whole percent here and a fraction on the wire

The native editing model (`OKTRecurringItem.recurringRate`) is an
integer 0-100, and its even-split rule depends on integer division and
remainder (`100/n` with the remainder spread over the tail, e.g. six
coins become 16/16/17/17/17/17). Holding the same integer keeps that
arithmetic exact and keeps Rust's rounding identical to the shipped
behaviour. The order endpoint wants a decimal fraction, so
[`to_order_coin_params`] converts on the way out — by integer
formatting, never through a float.
One coin's allocation, for the batch write [`RecurringBuyPlaceOrderActions::set_coin_ratios`].

Deliberately carries ONLY the ratio. `RecurringSelectedCoin` would compile here
but also carries `min_price`/`max_price`, and a caller that does not know about
price bounds would blank them on every write. Recurring's bounds currently live
only in the ObjC mirror, so that would be latent rather than live — but a record
that cannot express the mistake is better than one that relies on the field
staying unused.

`ratio_percent` is whole percent, matching `RecurringSelectedCoin`. No decimal
fraction crosses here — that conversion belongs to `apply_recommendation`, which
receives a *server* plan.

name: execute_stop_with_options
doc:
Execute the stop with full, explicit control over which optional
wire fields are present. Additive sibling to [`Self::execute_stop`] /
[`Self::execute_stop_with_condition`] — those two always emit
`instId` and `algoOrdType` (when the interactor holds them) and
require a concrete `StopType`, which cannot represent legacy Smart
Arbitrage's two stop paths:

- `BotOperatorButtonDisposer`'s minimal "close bots" dispatch sends
`StrategyStopReq(algoId)` alone — no `instId`, no `algoOrdType`,
no `stopType`.
- `SmartArbiStopConfirmDialog` sends `algoOrdType` but never
`instId`, and omits `stopType` for the sell-all case (only the
keep-staking case sends a concrete `stopType`).

Parameters:
- `stop_type = None` omits the `stopType` key entirely — distinct
from `Some(StopType::StopAndSell)`, which callers must not use as
an "omit" stand-in (that conflation is exactly the wire-parity
risk this method exists to remove, even though
`SmartArbStopRequestBody` happens to also omit the key for
`StopAndSell` today — see that type's doc comment). `Some(t)`
sends `t`'s wire value.
- `include_inst_id = false` omits `instId` even though the
interactor was constructed with a real `inst_id` — both Smart
Arbitrage stop paths never populate `instId` on the legacy
request.
- `include_ord_type = false` omits `algoOrdType` — only the minimal
"close bots" path needs this; the confirm-dialog path keeps it.

Grid/DCA and any existing caller of the plain two methods are
unaffected — this method's behavior is opt-in per call site.

fields.name: convertors
fields.doc:
Role-keyed display convertors for this instrument + the user's size-unit
setting, applied by native to the raw values it already holds.

`None` means NOT YET RESOLVED — native must keep its legacy formatting
until a set arrives. This is deliberately an `Option` rather than a
defaulted value: `ContractDcaConvertors::default()` carries `precision: 0`,
which both renderers apply as max-fraction-digits, so publishing it would
TRUNCATE every price and size to an integer (`62183.45` -> `62,183`,
`0.0035` -> `0`) rather than pass values through. Precision 0 is also a
legitimate resolved value for a contract size, so native cannot tell the
two apart from the number alone — the absence has to be modelled.

Resolution is retried until it succeeds: the `instId` may arrive with
bot_info rather than the nav param (Android seeds it empty), and on a
cold-process deeplink the shared instrument store is not warm yet. See
`resolve_convertors_for`.

This is the replacement for native deciding precision/rounding/unit off
its own OKTradeCore convertors — see
`docs/rfcs/detail-convertor-surface.md`. It does NOT replace `raw_json`:
the blob stays as the VALUE path (§1.2), this fixes only the FORMAT path.

is a forbidden native authority there (`TacticsDetailsActivity.kt:1075-1101`).

what UniFFI emits for an Object. Rust-side consumers use `inner()`
to project back to the trait Arc.

name: bot_stop_service
doc:
Hand off this bot's stop service for injection into a
`StopBotInteractor`. Native composes:
```ignore
let handle = OKTSSmartArbitrageService::new().bot_stop_service();
let interactor = StopBotInteractor::create(algo_id, inst_id, StopBotType::SmartArbitrage, handle);
```
Native must NOT call `interactor.start()` for Smart Arbitrage — it
has no precompute-stop endpoint (`action_service.rs`'s
`BotStopServiceTrait::fetch_precompute_stop` returns `Ok(vec![])`
defensively if it's ever called anyway, mirroring the existing
force-sell skip-`start()` convention). Call `execute_stop` /
`execute_stop_with_condition` directly instead.
